ambiguities.description: Both 'spend tier' and 'risk tier' are called 'tier' by different stakeholders causing confusion. The model uses SpendTier and RiskTier as distinct value types/fields to disambiguate, but the naming convention is not consistently adopted by staff in practice.

source_references.excerpt:
And you both call it "tier."
... We've asked people to say spend tier and risk tier. Nobody does.

ambiguities.description: Tax ID is mentioned as a vendor property but is explicitly not unique (duplicates exist). Should Tax ID still be modeled as a value type property of Vendor even though it cannot serve as an identifier, and should the known duplicate-vendor cleanup issue affect how it's constrained (e.g., no uniqueness constraint should be applied)?

source_references.excerpt:
Facilitator: And could you identify a vendor by tax ID instead?
Dana: You'd think so, but no. We have vendors with the same tax ID...
Facilitator: Noted, but out of scope for today. Tax ID isn't an identifier, vendor number is.

ambiguities.description: The vendor has three addresses (remit-to, ship-from, legal) described as 'frequently different and frequently wrong.' It's unclear if these should be modeled as three separate value types/roles or as a single Address concept with an address-type role. The transcript doesn't clarify structure (street/city/etc.) either.

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: Duplicate vendor records exist (same legal entity onboarded twice, or related entities under one parent). This is flagged as a known data quality/compliance issue but no rule was defined to prevent or resolve duplication within today's session, so no constraint was modeled for it.

source_references.excerpt:
We have vendors with the same tax ID -- different legal entities under one parent that file together, or we've onboarded the same company twice by accident and nobody's merged them.
... There's a cleanup project that's been on the roadmap for two years.
... The duplicates are also a compliance problem

ambiguities.description: The post-suspension handling of in-flight Purchase Orders (a potential 'run-off' status) was explicitly left unresolved and deferred to a steering group / Legal. No constraint models what happens to POs when a vendor transitions to suspended.

source_references.excerpt: If we suspend a vendor... what happens to the purchase orders already in flight?... Then we need a middle state. Something like run-off... This goes to the sourcing steering group.

ambiguities.description: The 'preferred vendor' flag exists informally in Mei's personal spreadsheet with no defined rule or criteria, and was explicitly excluded from modeling per stakeholder request. Confirmed as out of scope, not modeled.

source_references.excerpt: There's a column called "preferred."... I'm going to note that as a gap rather than a rule... It's ad hoc. Don't model it.

ambiguities.description: Region count is stated as 'four today' with talk of splitting EMEA, implying the value constraint for RegionCode may change in the future. Should the value constraint be treated as fixed or subject to change/versioning?

source_references.excerpt:
Region code. EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM.
... Four today. There's been talk of splitting EMEA but it hasn't happened.

ambiguities.description: Whether a vendor's risk review history (multiple review records over time, only one 'current') requires an explicit 'is_current' flag or effective-dating attribute on the Review entity was implied but not fully specified structurally (e.g., no field name given for marking a review as current/signed-off beyond 'signed off').

source_references.excerpt:
A vendor accumulates review records over time. At most one is the current one. Being active requires a current signed-off review.
... The review is its own record. It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when
